rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Stefan–Boltzmann's law**: a black body radiates $E = \sigma T^4$ per unit area, with $\sigma = 5.67 \times 10^{-8}$ W m⁻²K⁻⁴; real bodies emit $e\sigma T^4$ with emissivity e. In surroundings at T_s the net loss is $e\sigma A(T^4 - T_s^4)$ — the difference of fourth powers, with T always absolute.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - E = σT⁴; dQ/dt = eσAT⁴ - Net: dQ/dt = eσA(T⁴ − T_s⁴) - σ = 5.67×10⁻⁸ W m⁻²K⁻⁴

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Absolute temperature only** — Celsius values must be converted before raising to the fourth power.  ·  **Net exchange uses T⁴ − T_s⁴**, not (T − T_s)⁴.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The fourth power is why small temperature changes have huge radiative consequences.**

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: E = σT⁴; σ = 5.67×10⁻⁸ W m⁻²K⁻⁴; net: eσA(T⁴ − T_s⁴).  ·  T → 2T multiplies power by 16.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Earth's equilibrium: absorbing ~239 W/m² of averaged sunlight ⇒ radiating at T ≈ 255 K — the greenhouse effect raises the surface to ~288 K.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The T⁴ Rule Double a body's absolute temperature and its radiated power multiplies by sixteen. That brutal fourth-power dependence — Stefan–Boltzmann's law — sets the energy budget of planets, stars and furnaces, and explains why a few degrees of global warming matters so much.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2024) ### 2.1 Statement **The total energy radiated per second per unit surface area of a perfect black body is directly proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature:** $$E = \sigma T^4$$ with $\sigma = 5.67 \times 10^{-8}$ W m⁻²K⁻⁴ (Stefan's constant).…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 59:** Stefan's law is the integrated black-body spectrum. - **To Newton's cooling (Topic 50):** for small (T − T_s), $T^4 - T_s^4 \approx 4T_s^3(T - T_s)$ — Newton's law emerges as the small-excess limit.…
